title: 7 Times the World Almost Ended
description:
Welcome to Tab Twelve, where we go deeper down the internet.

During the Cold War, and after it, the world came close to nuclear war again and again, and some of the triggers will surprise you. A radar echo off the Moon. A bear climbing a fence. A B-52 that broke apart over North Carolina with two hydrogen bombs on board. A practice attack loaded onto the live system, and a computer chip worth 46 cents. A Norwegian science rocket. Sunlight on clouds. And a Soviet submarine, cut off and overheating, with a nuclear torpedo on board. This is the countdown of the seven times the world almost ended, and the full story behind each one, including what the legends leave out.

Released on Remembrance Day. We remember everyone who served.

title: GTA 6 Leaked for a Crypto Coin
description:
Welcome to Tab Twelve, deeper down the internet.

On October 10th, 2026, an anonymous leaker called Cyberleek posted a ransom note. If a new crypto coin hit a $30 million market value, the whole of GTA 6 would be released, 40 days before launch. This is how the most guarded game in the world kept leaking, from the 2022 Rockstar hack to a box with no disc inside, and how the leaks turned into a business. Protester or scammer? You decide.

title: What Does Palantir Actually Do?
description:
Welcome to Tab Twelve, deeper down the internet.

Palantir is worth hundreds of billions of dollars, and most people can't say what it does. Its software sits behind an ICE tool that maps deportation targets, the Pentagon's Maven Smart System, and hospital systems in Florida and England. This episode looks at what Palantir actually builds, the case for worry, the case for the future, and the one question both sides are really arguing about.

title: RuneScape Gold vs the Bolívar
description:

title: The Animals We Sent to War
description:
Dogs have officially served in the US military since 1942, and they are one of the least surprising animals ever sent to war. The CIA wired a cat with a microphone and a transmitter. Armed bats set part of an American airfield on fire. Pigeons were trained to steer a missile. A messenger pigeon called Cher Ami became a legend. Polish soldiers adopted a bear, and the Marines made a horse a staff sergeant. This episode also covers the Soviet anti-tank dogs, the horses of the First World War, a Newfoundland dog named Gander, and the dolphins and rats that are still working today. Some of these stories sound almost fun. But the animals weren't volunteers.

title: Could AI End the World?
description:
In September 2026, AI researcher Jacob Coxon quit his job at Anthropic and warned that AI could kill us all by the end of the decade. So could it actually happen? This episode looks at the three ways AI could go wrong, losing control, misuse and slow damage, and then at what we could gain if it goes right.
